T–S · Question 1 — M2 Activation
It's Monday morning. Your US colleague asks: "So, what does your typical week look like?" — Describe 3 things you always, usually, or never do. Use Simple Present.
S–S · Question 2 — Small Talk
You're at the coffee machine with a colleague you just met. Make small talk for 30 seconds — no silence allowed. Ask about their routine, their job, what they like about the company. Use Wh-questions.
Class · Question 3 — Time Check
Go around the room: each person says what time they start work, what time they finish, and one thing they always do before lunch. Use: "I start at… / I finish at… / I always…"
Teacher Note
Write 4–5 student sentences on the board. Underline the adverbs of frequency. Watch for: "I am always check emails" ✗ → adverb goes BETWEEN subject and verb, NOT before to be. Collect for §5.
⚡ Quick Win — 20 seconds
Say out loud: "I always start at nine. I usually check emails first. I never skip lunch." — Three adverbs. Three facts. Thirty seconds.
5 min · 3 questions · Badge 📅 when done
§2
Speaking · A Week at Vertex Logistics
3 rounds · Routines · Small talk · Problem-solving in context
8–10 min
T–S
Ana García — Week 2 at Vertex. Her US manager David calls and asks: "Ana, what do you usually do on Monday mornings?"
Describe Ana's Monday routine: 4 things she always/usually/sometimes does. Use Simple Present + frequency adverbs.

"I always arrive at 8:45. I usually check my emails first — there are always messages from Chicago. I sometimes have a team standup at 9. I never skip the standup — it's important."

always/usually/sometimes/never — position: BEFORE main verb, AFTER to be

S–S
Coffee machine, 10 AM. Partner A is a new colleague. Make 60 seconds of real small talk — ask about their job, their routine, something they like about Vertex. No silence. Use Wh-questions + Simple Present.

"What department do you work in? Oh, operations! Do you usually work early? I'm not a morning person — I always need coffee first! What do you like about working here?"

GT Original: "I'm not a morning person" — M2 colloquial applied in M6 context

Class
End-of-week problem. It's Friday 5 PM. Each student has ONE work problem this week — something they don't usually do, something that's broken, or something they can't find. Report it in 2 sentences to the class.

"I don't usually work late, but this week I always work until 7. There's a problem with my computer — the screen doesn't work. I need IT support, please."

Simple Present negative + there is/are + can/need — M2+M4+M5 in one problem report

Teacher Note — Frequency Adverb Drill
After Round 1, quick board drill: "Where does ALWAYS go in this sentence?" Write: "I ___ check emails" vs "I am ___ busy". Students place the adverb. This is the #1 positioning error at A1.1 and it must be automatic by M6.

Teacher Note — "available" vs S1A usage
Students saw "available" in S1A for meeting rooms. Now it applies to people. Same word, two contexts. Ask: "In S1A, what was available? Now, who is available?" This cross-session connection reinforces retention.

Use 4 words from the list in real sentences about your job. Include at least one adverb of frequency.
Model: "I have two meetings on Mondays. My deadline is usually Friday. I'm always busy in the morning. I'm not available for calls before 9."

§4
Colloquial · 4 Phrases for Office Small Talk
Monday catch-up · routine chat · professional but natural
5 min
"How was your weekend?"
The universal Monday opener in English-speaking companies. Always ask — it builds rapport fast.
A: "How was your weekend?" B: "Good, thanks! Yours?"
"I'm swamped." / "I'm slammed."
Native way to say "estoy hasta la madre de trabajo." Very common in corporate English — use it confidently.
"Can you help me?" — "Sorry, I'm totally swamped today."
"I'm OOO on Friday."
OOO = Out Of Office. Essential in any company with US/international contact. Use in emails and WhatsApp.
"Just so you know — I'm OOO on Friday. Email me Monday."
"Let me check my schedule."
Buys time professionally when someone asks if you're free. Natural, polite, and very common.
"Are you free Tuesday at 2?" — "Let me check my schedule."
Teacher Note — Monday Morning Chain Drill
Chain around the room: Student A asks "How was your weekend?" → B answers + says "I'm swamped this week" → C asks "Are you free Thursday?" → D responds "Let me check my schedule… I'm OOO Friday." One circuit. Fast. Natural.
§5
Grammar · Simple Present + Adverbs of Frequency
Problem → Tool · Position rules · Wh-questions in context · Poll + 2 Activities
10–12 min
🚨 Real Situation — The Standup Question
Your Chicago manager asks during the Monday standup: "Do you usually work overtime? How often do you have meetings?"
You want to say: "A veces hago horas extra. Siempre tengo junta los lunes. Nunca llego tarde."
❓ How do you place the adverbs correctly in English — and where does "How often" go?
✅ Two Rules — Position is Everything
Rule 1 — Main verb: Subject + adverb + verb → "I always check emails." / "She never works overtime."
Rule 2 — To be: Subject + to be + adverb → "I am always busy." / "He is usually late." — adverb AFTER to be!
Rule 3 — Questions: "How often do you…?" → Answer with frequency: "I usually…" / "twice a week" / "every Monday"
Adverb% frequencyWith main verbWith to be
always100%I always check emails first.I am always busy on Mondays.
usually~80%She usually arrives at 9.She is usually on time.
sometimes~50%We sometimes work overtime.The room is sometimes full.
never0%I never skip the standup.He is never available on Fridays.
⚠️ Top 3 position errors — catch them every time:
✘ "I check always my emails" → ✅ I always check my emails — adverb before verb
✘ "I am never late" → ✅ correct! — but students often say "I never am late" ✗ — after to be
✘ "How often you have meetings?" → ✅ How often do you have meetings? — do/does in questions
⚡ Quick Poll — 3 Grammar Questions
Loading...
✏️ Activity A — Put the Adverb in the Right Place
1. She ___ arrives late to the Monday standup. (never)
2. The meeting room is ___ available on Friday afternoons. (usually)
3. ___ do you check your emails? — Every morning.
4. I ___ have a break at 10 — the coffee machine is always busy after that! (sometimes)
🗣️ Micro-Speaking — 60 seconds
Tell your partner your real work routine using all 4 adverbs: always / usually / sometimes / never. Partner listens and marks the adverb position — before main verb or after to be?
✏️ Activity B — True or False? Adverb Position Rules
"I always am late" — adverb in correct position with to be.
"How often do you have meetings?" — correct question structure.
"She usually works from home on Fridays" — adverb is correctly placed.
"I never don't eat lunch" — correct way to say "nunca salto el almuerzo".
§6
Listening · David's Monday Morning Update
Routine + problems + small talk · All structures integrated · Badge 🎧
8–10 min
David's Monday Update — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M6 · S2A · Voice: ElevenLabs · Speed: 0.78
0:00 0:00

Good morning, everyone. My name is David Torres, and I'm the operations manager here at Vertex Logistics in Celaya. I usually start work at 8:30, but on Mondays I always arrive at 8 because we have a team standup at 8:15. I never miss the standup — it's the most important part of my week.

My schedule this week is very busy. I always have three meetings on Mondays. Today I have a call with Chicago at 10, a supplier meeting at 2, and a department review at 4. I sometimes work overtime on Mondays, but I try not to.

There's a small problem this morning. The printer in my office doesn't work — it's broken again. I always print the meeting agenda before the standup, but today I can't. I need IT support. The IT department is sometimes slow on Mondays because everyone has problems at the same time!

My new colleague Ana is also here today — it's her second week. She usually arrives at 8:45, and she's always very organized. She already has her schedule for the whole week! She's not available on Wednesday afternoon — she has a training session. I never forget to check her calendar before I schedule meetings.

Okay — it's 8:13 now. The standup starts in two minutes. How was your weekend? Mine was great — very relaxing. Let's have a good week!

📎 ElevenLabs: Voice — David (American English) · Speed 0.78 · A1.1 M6 S2A · ~185 words

Teacher Note — Listening Task
Pre-listening: "Count how many adverbs of frequency you hear. Write them down." Students listen once for gist. Second listen: comprehension questions. After: compare adverb lists — who found all 9? (always ×4, usually ×3, sometimes ×2, never ×3)
1. What time does David usually start work?
2. What is the problem this morning?
3. True or False: Ana is available on Wednesday afternoon.
4. True or False: David sometimes works overtime on Mondays.

I can ask "How often do you…?" and answer with a frequency expression.

"How was your weekend?"
Say this to one English-speaking colleague on Monday. It costs nothing and builds everything.
"I'm swamped / I'm OOO Friday."
Use one of these in a real email or WhatsApp this week. Native, natural, zero translation needed.
"Let me check my schedule."
Next time someone asks if you're free, say this instead of "yes" or "no". Professional and buys you time.
